description:
Objective
Establish one shared, extensible capability-snapshot contract and normalization path across EmailBridge, JidoChatBridge and WebBridge. File delivery is the first extension, not the boundary of this design. Bridges translate adapter declarations; shared consumers must not branch on bridge or provider identity.

Current gap and scope
EmailBridge supplies file_delivery metadata, while JidoChatBridge and WebBridge do not project equivalent adapter metadata. Complete these paths in PR 2. This brings ZAQ bridge integration forward from zaq-h2i.4; that issue retains upstream adapter declarations and published dependency work. Do not copy SMTP's metadata values into other transports.

Implementation and acceptance
1. Build on Bridge.capability_snapshot/2 and CommunicationBridge.normalize_capability_snapshot/2. Normalize the whole communication capability snapshot through one shared path, including existing capability statuses and the file_delivery section. Keep domain-specific validation in existing owning helpers such as ConnectorConfig.FileSettings. Avoid a second competing normalization pipeline.
2. Bridges supply minimal transport/adapter declarations, not repeated default maps or independent normalization. Obtain facts dynamically from the selected Jido/Web adapter where its contract supports them; retain Email's appropriate transport declarations. Preserve selected connection/adapter identity.
3. Centralize shape validation and conservative default handling. Preserve native/fallback/unsupported meanings and distinguish unsupported, unresolved and explicitly not-applicable facts. Missing metadata must not imply attachment support, unlimited limits, or configurable/required controls. configurable: true and required: true require explicit transport declarations. Generic message-edit support does not prove attachment-edit support.
4. Use the same normalized snapshot in the capability endpoint, BO settings and TransportRequirements.resolve/2. Keep channel policy/configuration separate from adapter facts. Bridges must not build TransportRequirements. Fixed transport ceilings cannot be raised by configuration.
5. Future capability sections must be able to extend this shared contract without another normalization implementation per bridge. Document ownership and the extension point; implement only current capabilities and file delivery. Do not build a speculative registry, plugin framework, future settings or generic operation dispatcher.
6. Inspect actual adapter APIs before selecting a metadata source. The installed Jido dependency has no established structured file-metadata API. Record the smallest explicit source contract/prerequisite; do not insert structured metadata into Jido's status-only capability matrix or hide an invented fallback. No new parallel bridge file_delivery_capabilities callback.
7. Preserve unrelated Jido/Mattermost capability declarations and behavior. Do not edit ignored dependencies, bump pins or invent transport limits/modes. Do not add provider-name cases in shared normalization, BO or resolver. Actual attachment acquisition/planning/sending remains outside PR 2.

Validation
- Use TDD in existing owning test suites. Exercise the real Bridge capability-snapshot path for Email, Jido and Web, not only manually constructed snapshots.
- Prove consistent normalized semantics across bridges, preservation of existing statuses, safe absent metadata and rejection of malformed metadata.
- Use contract-compatible test adapters to prove selected-adapter isolation and dynamic fixed/configurable/required limits, transfer mode and attachment-edit support.
- Prove declared metadata reaches the shared BO settings and requirements resolver without provider-specific consumer edits, including fixed-ceiling enforcement and configuration precedence.
- Verify SMTP-specific required encoded-message/count settings are not imposed on Web or Jido by default. Metadata alone must not enable unimplemented sending.
- Cover normalization invariants with property tests where appropriate; preserve unrelated assertions.

Action reuse assessment
Extend the existing bridge capability_snapshot/1 producers and shared snapshot normalization. Reuse Bridge.capability_snapshot/2, CommunicationBridge, FileSettings, the existing capability endpoint, NodeRouter/Event boundary and TransportRequirements.resolve/2. No new Action, endpoint or agent tool is needed.

Implementation prompt
Work in ../zaq-feat-channel-file-settings on feat/channel-file-settings, PR jat10/zaq#16 stacked on feat/email-capabilities. Verify current Git state and preserve other work. Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/services/channels.md, docs/testing-approach.md and docs/code-quality.md; read DESIGN.md and docs/bo-components.md before affected UI work. Use Serena for source navigation.
Write failing tests first, implement the smallest coherent change, run focused regressions and mix q, and update this issue with evidence and remaining dependency gaps. Reuse existing test modules, fixtures and setup; create a module only when no suitable owner exists and explain why. Write original tests, do not copy old-worktree tests or weaken assertions, and follow existing-test approval rules. Do not run mix precommit, commit, push or merge without fresh authorization.
title: [zaq-h2i.3.8] Unify capability snapshot normalization across Email, Jido and Web bridges
